name: Chicken, Leek, Carrot & Celery Pie
description: Flour-coated chicken breast with leek, carrot and celery in a light cream and mustard sauce beneath crisp shortcrust pastry.

instructions: Cut the chicken into roughly 3 cm pieces, season and roll lightly in 15 g plain flour. Brown in 1 tbsp olive oil, then continue cooking until the centre reaches 75°C; transfer to a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pan. Add the leek, carrot, celery and dried thyme, then cook for 8–10 minutes until softened.

Gradually stir in 150 ml prepared chicken stock and simmer until thickened. Stir in the double cream and 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard, then return the cooked chicken only long enough to coat it and bring the filling back to a simmer.
make_ahead.storage: Cool promptly in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate within two hours for up to 48 hours.
day_of: Transfer the cold filling to a small pie dish while the oven heats to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan.
Top with the shortcrust pastry, trim and crimp, cut a steam hole and brush with beaten egg. Bake for 30–35 minutes until deeply golden and the filling is bubbling and steaming throughout.

instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan.
Season the chicken breast pieces with salt and black pepper. Roll them lightly in 15 g plain flour and shake off any excess.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 2-3 minutes per side, then transfer it to a plate; it does not need to be fully cooked yet.
Reduce the heat to medium and melt the butter in the same pan. Add the sliced leek, diced carrot, diced celery and dried thyme, then cook for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Dissolve the chicken stock cube in 150 ml boiling water. Gradually stir the stock into the vegetables, scraping the floury browned bits from the pan, and simmer until the sauce begins to thicken.
Stir in the double cream and 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard. Return the chicken and its resting juices, simmer for 2 minutes, then season to taste.
Transfer the filling to a small pie dish and leave it to cool for about 10 minutes so it does not soften the pastry.
Lay the shortcrust pastry over the filling, trim and crimp the edges, cut a steam hole in the centre and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is crisp and deeply golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
